response.markdown_report:
**Prioritize a dependency-light, mutation-tested BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter.** At 0% research progress, reliable measurements provide a stronger foundation than another unverified training intervention. This proposal measures diagnostic reliability; recommendation gains require separate host validation.

**Insights from the supplied evidence**

1. All four latest diagnostic runs failed on missing SciPy despite passing sampler and exported-serving checks. Isolated probes would preserve completed measurements and report actual blockers.
2. Electronics’ recent-deletion diagnostic hit@10 change was −0.125, with a descriptive interval excluding zero. This motivates investigation, without establishing validation benefit or a desirable sensitivity level.
3. Qualitative feedback distinguishes broad relevance from immediate suitability. Compatibility, ownership and mood remain unobserved; unidentified recommendations require abstention rather than negative labels.

**Insights from related work**

1. BERT4Rec [1] requires masked-target training and appended-MASK readout. Independent position-coded fixtures can detect indexing errors shared by production and exported implementations.
2. ModelMeta [2] tests framework correctness through equivalent executions. DeepMutation, DeepCrime and probabilistic mutation testing [4–6] motivate fault coverage and control-error measurement, without establishing recommendation gains.
3. Sampled-ranking research [3] shows candidate sampling can change model comparisons. Training-prefix audits must remain separate from pinned host validation.

The resulting directions are contract verification, candidate-difficulty auditing, and evidence-aware qualitative annotation.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract verification | Successful numerical parity | Independent fixtures and isolated mutations | Unspecified faults and shared mistakes |
| Candidate difficulty | Random-negative margins | Frequency/lexical distractor audit | Unknown distractor relevance |
| Qualitative evidence | Twenty training users | Evidence spans and abstention labels | Limited population coverage |

**Candidate ideas** — scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutation-tested adapter [1,2,4–6] | 3/7/6 | Concrete synthesis; reusable checks; bounded fixtures | Established methods; indirect accuracy value; state isolation is demanding |
| Candidate-difficulty audit [3] | 4/6/5 | Exposes ranking difficulty; reusable strata; frozen-model execution | Familiar audit; uncertain training benefit; pool construction costs |
| Evidence-aware feedback schema | 3/5/3 | Separates abstention; improves interpretation; simple records | Limited novelty; sparse coverage; independent annotation effort |

**Selected algorithm.** Preserve the corrected baseline and train exactly one BERT4Rec per category. Each probe independently returns PASS, FAIL, UNAVAILABLE or ERROR with measurements, denominators and definitions. Recompute gates from current results; isolate optional dependencies.

```python
batches = immutable_cache_of_already_consumed_training_batches()
for probe in registered_probes:
    results[probe.name] = run_isolated(probe, view, batches)
for fault in preregistered_faults:
    results[fault] = compare_control_and_disposable_mutant(fault, fixtures)
return {"metrics": results, "metric_definitions": definitions}
```

Use position-coded readout fixtures, independently calculated attention outputs, and authoritative routing checks. Mutate readout, padding masking, reserved-mask handling, visible targets and checkpoint consistency; additionally combine readout/padding faults. Report detected/eligible nonequivalent mutants, unresolved survivors, unchanged-control false alarms/control runs, uncertainty and runtime. Survivors do not establish equivalence.

Use cached batches without advancing training iterators. Restore individual module modes, controlled RNGs, buffers and hooks. Fix tolerances before mutation evaluation and hold back fixture variants to limit fixture overfitting. Preserve ModelView, predictor consistency, fixed seeds, four routes, 200 batches/epoch and at most 200 epochs. Cap all diagnostic costs within the shared budget; select solely through host macro validation HR@10. No validation gain is claimed.

idea.description: Build a dependency-light, mutation-tested diagnostic adapter for the supplied corrected BERT4Rec, preserving one independently trained model and one deployed checkpoint per category. Establish fault-specific diagnostic sensitivity and unchanged-control specificity using independent fixtures before interpreting measurements as grounds for training changes.
idea.motivation: The latest supplied runs passed sampler and exported-serving parity checks but failed with a missing SciPy dependency; residual-patching messages incorrectly continued to cite prerequisite failures. Earlier runs exposed missing category identity. These establish measurement and integration problems, while no supplied host validation result demonstrates a training repair. The revised proposal prioritizes reliable partial results, independent oracles and reproducible diagnostic execution.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every supplied ModelView interface. Use view.model as the actual trained network. Preserve the corrected baseline architecture, family-specific sample_batch, sampler, loss and serving computation for this first intervention. The loader compatibility contract remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors.

Represent each probe result with PASS, FAIL, UNAVAILABLE or ERROR, measured values, observation counts, definition, tolerances, dependencies and a specific reason where applicable. FAIL means a measured contract violation; ERROR means execution failed; UNAVAILABLE means required evidence or prerequisites are absent. Catch exceptions at individual probe boundaries and preserve completed results. Recompute downstream gate reasons from current results, including exception details. Use PyTorch and the standard library for core checks; avoid eager optional imports. Missing SciPy disables only dependent statistics. Do not silently substitute a different statistical procedure.

Preregister a versioned protocol containing faults, fixtures, expected relations, category mapping source, checkpoint hashes, software/backend versions, precision, tolerances, repeat counts, denominator rules, diagnostic cap and deterministic fixture seeds. Separate development fixtures from locked evaluation variants. Declare a finite repeat count before evaluation, such as ten unchanged-control executions per fixture/category on the recorded backend. Repetition measures execution stability conditional on that setup; it does not provide independent user or model samples.

Use fixed, independently cloned batches captured from batches that training already consumes. Do not populate the diagnostic cache by advancing the training iterator or creating another iterator from the same loader. Preserve the public run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) signature by passing a replay loader over these cached tuples. If no cache exists, use an isolated dataset/loader with dedicated generators and documented sampling state, without sharing live worker processes or mutable dataset instances. Cache tensors separately and prevent probes from modifying them. Parent RNG restoration cannot rewind multiprocessing workers, prefetch queues, persistent dataset state or custom sampler cursors.

Snapshot Python, NumPy, default Torch CPU and relevant CUDA RNG states plus all dedicated diagnostic generators. Record every submodule's training flag, enter evaluation mode and suppress gradients for ordinary forward probes; gradient suppression alone does not disable dropout. Restore individual flags rather than recursively calling train() with one global flag. Audit custom forwards and pre-existing hooks for mutation. Protect cloned persistent and nonpersistent buffers and other explicitly identified mutable state; state_dict() alone omits nonpersistent buffers and un-cloned tensors can alias live state. Avoid backward calls and optimizer updates. Use try/finally to remove only diagnostic-owned hooks, restore protected state and controlled RNGs, undo mutations and release activation references. If complete state isolation cannot be guaranteed, report the affected probe unavailable or run it in a disposable diagnostic copy of the same checkpoint; never independently train that copy.

Check reserved tokens, real-item labels and masked supervised positions from loader tensors. Explicitly state that tensors alone cannot establish prefix provenance or the negative-sampling distribution. Check provenance through sampler instrumentation or controlled fixtures with known source windows; unavailable instrumentation must remain unavailable. Earlier repeated item identities are legitimate history and must not automatically be treated as leakage. Add a deliberately visible supervised-target fault, and require the corruption-contract probe to reject it even if its scores appear plausible.

Verify category identity, item mapping and serialized architecture metadata against authoritative host/training-loop routing information before numerical parity. Merely comparing mutually consistent artifact fields is insufficient. Pass the actual category explicitly into ModelView. Test routing with category-specific sentinel fixtures or a deliberately mismatched route/manifest; do not load another trial's checkpoint. If two routes are behaviorally indistinguishable on a fixture, record inconclusive numerical discrimination and retain the independent identity check.

Compare the current model with a freshly loaded exported category checkpoint, including exact state-tensor identity, dtype and shape, finite features/logits and ordered rankings across short, mixed-length, full-length, truncated and batched histories. Add batch-permutation and candidate-permutation checks in evaluation mode, keeping item IDs paired with their scores. Use an independent diagnostic ordering rule of descending score then ascending item ID; do not change host tie handling. Numerical agreement alone cannot establish correct routing or absence of shared leakage.

Construct an independent readout fixture with length-six input [0,0,0,a,b,MASK] and distinct position-coded encoder features. Assert that the selected vector is exactly the position-five feature; count(nonpadding)-1 incorrectly selects position two. Do not reuse production indexing helpers in the oracle. Include mixed history lengths, maxlen-1 histories and histories requiring truncation before appending MASK. For real-model checks, independently gather the final-MASK feature and compare candidate logits. Serving retains the latest maxlen-1 interactions, appends reserved MASK, and reads its actual final nonpadding index, never count-1. Reject malformed fixtures without a valid MASK readout. Exclude PAD and MASK from recommendation candidates.

For attention padding, preserve sequence length, real-token IDs, their absolute positions and the original boolean key-padding mask. Perturb only padded hidden states immediately before attention and require valid outputs and MASK logits to remain unchanged. Do not move real tokens by adding/removing left padding: learned absolute positions make that a different input. Choose perturbations that survive zeroing and LayerNorm. Supplement the real-model relation with a deterministic attention fixture: zero query/key projections produce uniform attention over eligible keys, distinct projected padded values expose disabled masking, and an independent arithmetic mean over valid values provides the oracle. Verify the actual attention implementation's mask convention; PyTorch MultiheadAttention uses True to ignore a key.

Run numerical checks in evaluation mode, FP32 and without autocast; require finite outputs. Preserve existing serialized-serving thresholds of atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 for continuity, recording them explicitly. For new deterministic fixtures, begin with atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5, calibrate against unchanged repeat-run/backend noise using development fixtures, and freeze thresholds before locked mutation evaluation. Engineer mutant differences comfortably above tolerance. Record absolute and relative discrepancies, checking features and logits as well as rankings; unchanged top-k lists can conceal defects. Exact position-coded and metadata assertions do not require a floating-point tolerance.

Preregister isolated mutations for count-1 readout, disabled key-padding masking, reserved-mask handling, visible supervised targets and checkpoint/predictor consistency. Include readout and padding mutations together as a separate interaction case. Define each mutation's precise code site, intended effect, relevant probe and discriminating fixture. Establish control acceptance first, then run a single mutant, restore it and verify restoration before continuing. Mutation wrappers or copies must use the category's existing model/checkpoint and must never reach deployed artifacts. Do not mutate production checkpoint files or fuse scores.

Report per-fault and per-category counts: constructed, eligible, detected, surviving, demonstrably equivalent, unresolved, unavailable and errored. Define detection coverage as detected eligible nonequivalent mutants divided by eligible nonequivalent mutants. Declare nonequivalence using an independent discriminating fixture or justified structural argument, not the detector's own verdict. A surviving mutant is not thereby equivalent. Exclude demonstrably equivalent cases only with explicit justification, and retain unresolved survivors visibly outside the coverage denominator. Errors and missing evidence never count as detections.

Define unchanged-control false-positive rate as false alarms divided by completed eligible unchanged-control runs under the same protocol. Report numerator, denominator and a prespecified descriptive 95% Wilson interval when the denominator is nonzero; use null otherwise. This is an experiment-specific operational measure, not a universal metric attributed to the cited mutation papers. Repeated deterministic runs are dependent evidence about stability, so avoid population-level specificity claims or interpreting a narrow interval as broad fault coverage. Report detection coverage as a finite declared-suite result rather than a representative sample of all possible defects.

Generate diagnosis_interpreter_prompt directly from measured results, definitions, denominators, availability and costs. Distinguish partial completion, untested contracts and hypotheses. Preserve existing valid behavioral and margin probes; defer residual patching until core execution succeeds. Do not infer collapse from embedding scores near 0.5, convergence from positive training margins, validation quality from training-prefix hits, or user preferences from perturbation sensitivity. Qualitative records should separate immediate choice, deferred relevance, explicit mismatch, redundancy and unidentified-item abstention, with evidence spans and counts. Compatibility, ownership, quantity needs and mood require explicit evidence and remain unobserved when absent.

The main shortcut risk is diagnostic fixture overfitting: hard-coded expectations or production helpers reused as oracles can create false confidence. Use independently calculated expectations, locked fixture variants, mixed lengths, multiple candidate orders and combined faults. An unchanged adapter can still miss undeclared faults. Candidate-difficulty audits and evidence-aware annotations remain useful subsequent directions; neither supplies verified negative relevance labels or a validated training repair.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep checkpoint configuration, exported loading and the embedded predictor writer synchronized; this proposal changes no scoring architecture. Retain five real training users per category for full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable ratings, review content, prices, stores, item categories and simulator traits remain unavailable. Allocate a diagnostic cap within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget before execution and record warmup, loading, mutation, diagnostic, debugging and training costs. Stop at the cap with explicit incomplete results. Leave the pinned evaluator unchanged, select solely through four-category macro validation HR@10 and leave held-out evaluation to the host. Introduce no ensembles, auxiliary fitted scorers, checkpoint averaging or cross-trial checkpoint reuse.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Integration supplies a replay loader over independently cloned batches
        # captured from training's already-consumed batches; never advance its live iterator.
        saved = capture_individual_modes_controlled_rngs_and_mutable_state(self.view.model)
        metrics, definitions = {}, {}
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            batches = obtain_read_only_replay_batches_or_report_unavailable(train_loader)
            for probe in declared_dependency_order:
                definitions[probe.name] = probe.definition
                if diagnostic_cap_reached():
                    metrics[probe.name] = unavailable('Declared diagnostic cap reached')
                    continue
                blockers = current_unsatisfied_dependencies(probe, metrics)
                if blockers:
                    metrics[probe.name] = unavailable_with_specific_reasons(blockers)
                    continue
                try:
                    with torch.no_grad():
                        metrics[probe.name] = probe.measure(self.view, batches)
                except Exception as exc:
                    metrics[probe.name] = error_with_type_message_and_completed_counts(exc)

            for case in locked_mutation_protocol:
                definitions[case.name] = case.definition
                if diagnostic_cap_reached():
                    metrics[case.name] = unavailable('Declared diagnostic cap reached')
                    continue
                # Oracles are independent of production indexing/masking helpers.
                # Include position-coded readout and arithmetic attention fixtures.
                controls = run_declared_unchanged_control_repeats(case)
                if not controls.accepted:
                    metrics[case.name] = report_control_failure_without_claiming_detection(controls)
                    continue
                evidence = establish_nonequivalence_independently(case)
                try:
                    with disposable_fault_injection(case) as mutant:
                        outcome = run_relevant_probe_with_frozen_tolerances(case, mutant)
                finally:
                    restore_mutation_and_verify_control_state(case)
                metrics[case.name] = classify_detection_survival_equivalence_or_error(
                    controls, evidence, outcome)

            metrics['mutation_summary'] = summarize_declared_suite_counts(metrics)
            metrics['control_false_positive_rate'] = false_alarms_over_completed_controls(metrics)
            # Descriptive Wilson interval; disclose repeated-run dependence.
            metrics['diagnostic_cost'] = measured_cost_and_completion_status()
            return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
        finally:
            remove_only_diagnostic_owned_hooks()
            restore_mutable_state_individual_modes_and_controlled_rngs(self.view.model, saved)
            release_temporary_activation_references()


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return render_prompt_with_measured_metrics_definitions_and_denominators(
        raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish_partial_completion_and_unresolved_survivors=True,
        prohibit_unsupported_validation_mechanism_or_user_trait_claims=True)

# Preserve training/predictor architecture and all four category routes.
# Train/export exactly one corrected BERT4Rec per category.
# Temporary mutants are diagnostic executions of that model, never fitted predictors.
# Select solely through unchanged host macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Independent BERT4Rec contract fixtures, accurate partial-result reporting and fault-specific mutation evaluation form a useful task-specific synthesis.
originality.negative: Dependency isolation, metamorphic relations and mutation testing are established methods; the proposal introduces no new learning principle or general testing method.

future_potential.positive: A reliable adapter can support later objective, sampling and architecture experiments while detecting recurring integration failures and quantifying declared fault coverage.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic reliability does not directly improve recommendation accuracy, and success on a fixed mutation suite does not establish coverage of unknown defects.

code_difficulty.positive: Core fixtures use PyTorch and existing interfaces without changing or retraining the scoring architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent attention/readout oracles, loader isolation, mixed-mode and mutable-state restoration, authoritative routing checks and mutation accounting require substantial integration work.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item training for sequential recommendation.
Provides the objective foundation for masked-target construction and appended-MASK readout checks.
limitations: Does not establish correctness of the supplied harness implementation or diagnostic adapter.
Does not demonstrate benefits from the proposed mutation-tested diagnostics.

related_work.title: Improving Deep Learning Framework Testing with Model-Level Metamorphic Testing
contributions: Introduces ModelMeta, using output-preserving structural relations and interface transformations to test deep learning frameworks.
Uses adaptive transformation and seed selection, with oracles covering numerical behavior, resource use, execution time and crashes.
Motivates equivalent-execution checks such as batch and candidate permutation in the proposed adaptation.
limitations: Its subject is framework correctness; it provides no evidence of recommendation-accuracy improvements.
The proposed BERT4Rec checks are an adaptation, not an established benchmark from the paper.
Specified metamorphic relations cannot prove general correctness.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can change model comparisons.
Supports distinguishing diagnostic candidate audits from the fixed host evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned RecHarness evaluator.
Does not establish a beneficial training intervention for these four datasets.

related_work.title: DeepMutation: Mutation Testing of Deep Learning Systems
contributions: Defines source-level and model-level mutations for deep learning systems.
Introduces class-sensitive mutation assessment, supporting explicit fault-suite accounting.
limitations: Its class-sensitive score is not directly the proposed BERT4Rec contract-detection coverage.
Passing a selected mutation suite cannot establish general recommender correctness.

related_work.title: DeepCrime: Mutation Testing of Deep Learning Systems Based on Real Faults
contributions: Develops mutation operators informed by real deep learning faults.
Uses statistical killability and nontriviality considerations to distinguish meaningful mutation assessments.
limitations: Its training-based procedures are not reproduced by this bounded frozen-checkpoint diagnostic.
A surviving mutant does not establish behavioral equivalence.
Its mutation-score normalization should not be conflated with the proposed operational coverage measure.

related_work.title: A Probabilistic Framework for Mutation Testing in Deep Neural Networks
contributions: Addresses stochastic inconsistency in neural-network mutation assessment.
Motivates measuring unchanged-control false alarms and reporting execution variability.
limitations: Does not define the proposed experiment-specific unchanged-control false-positive rate as a universal metric.
Repeated fixed-checkpoint executions do not characterize uncertainty across trained models or users.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Specifies attention interfaces and boolean key-padding mask semantics.
Supports deterministic attention fixtures with independently calculated valid-key averages.
limitations: Custom attention implementations may use different mask conventions and require explicit verification.
API semantics alone do not verify the supplied model's attention wiring.

related_work.title: PyTorch DataLoader documentation
contributions: Documents worker seeding, multiprocessing, prefetching and persistent-worker behavior.
Supports replaying cached batches or using isolated diagnostic loaders to avoid perturbing training sampling.
limitations: Restoring parent RNG states does not rewind workers, queues or custom dataset state.
Application-specific samplers and mutable datasets require additional isolation.

related_work.title: PyTorch random number generation documentation
contributions: Documents default RNG state handling and fork_rng behavior.
Clarifies the need to track dedicated generators separately.
limitations: Default RNG restoration does not cover arbitrary generators, worker processes or sampler cursors.
Controlled RNGs alone do not ensure reproducibility across software versions and backends.

related_work.title: PyTorch Module documentation
contributions: Documents module modes, buffers, state serialization and hooks.
Supports explicit restoration of individual training flags and protected mutable state.
limitations: state_dict snapshots require cloning to avoid aliasing and omit nonpersistent buffers.
Custom Python state and existing hook side effects require application-specific auditing.

related_work.title: PyTorch inference_mode documentation
contributions: Documents inference-time gradient suppression.
Clarifies why gradient suppression and evaluation mode are separate execution controls.
limitations: Does not itself disable dropout, restore buffers or prevent custom forward mutations.
Its tensor restrictions require care when diagnostic values later enter other execution modes.

related_work.title: PyTorch testing documentation
contributions: Documents numerical comparison semantics and tolerance-based assertions.
Supports explicit feature/logit comparisons alongside ranking checks.
limitations: Suggested tolerances require calibration for the recorded model, precision and backend.
Numerical agreement cannot establish correct routing, provenance or absence of shared implementation errors.
